messages:
kevin: Heads-up: sample-apps started failing in CI after we bumped the SDK. Next middleware builds error with "MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Can't resolve 'fs'" even though app is running on Vercel Edge. anyone seen this?

tara: saw the same locally. root cause looks like bundler resolving the CJS path which pulls in node-only helpers. happens when import is static at module scope in middleware.

mohit: repro: create middleware that does `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'` at top-level. Next/Vite sometimes pick the require entry and then fails to resolve 'fs' during build.

kevin: quick workaround: dynamic import inside the middleware handler or explicitly import the edge entry: `import('@redwood/inference/edge')`. that fixes the bundler resolution.

tara: can we make the SDK pick the right file automatically? adding conditional exports in package.json would help: add an "edge" condition and a `./edge` subpath so older bundlers can explicitly use it.

mohit: agreed. also the SDK has a background token refresher that uses setInterval at module init which causes runtime errors in service-worker-like edge runtimes (setInterval not defined). we should guard timers and provide a fallback request-driven refresh.

kevin: filing a small patch: 1) add conditional exports + ./edge path, 2) build a tiny edge shim without timers or fs, 3) ship edge d.ts that avoids Node types. will open PR for review.

ui-bot: PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/428 (edge exports + edge build + types). CI queued.

mohit: typing note: projects that target lib: ["dom"] still get errors because SDK's index.d.ts references NodeJS.Timeout and Buffer. we should add an exports.types edge mapping so tsc picks edge-friendly types in edge contexts.

tara: small migration note for sample-apps and docs: until the patch lands, prefer `import('@redwood/inference/edge')` in middleware and avoid top-level imports. add a snippet showing how to do per-request token refresh if background refresh is disabled:```js
export default async function middleware(req) {
  const { createClient } = await import('@redwood/inference/edge');
  const client = createClient({ auth: { backgroundRefresh: false } });
  await client.refreshIfNeeded(req.headers.get('authorization'))
  // continue
}
```

kevin: release-bot: can we cut a rc once CI is green? this is blocking onboarding for a few customers.

release-bot: will cut 0.11.3-rc.1 after CI passes. linking issue #301 for followups (edge CI matrix + bundle tests).

mohit: follow-ups: add a bundle test job using Next and Vite in CI to prevent regressions, add unit tests that run in a service-worker-like runner (no timers, no process).

kevin: thanks all — once rc is published we'll update the examples and onboarding doc and notify the sample-app maintainers.
